Diabetes (glycemia / insulin resistance / pancreatic beta cells)

Small human trials and a 2026 systematic review report reductions in glucose, including HbA1c in the pooled literature. The review rated certainty very low to low, and durable glycemic control has not been established.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Small human trials and a 2026 systematic review report reductions in glucose, including HbA1c in the pooled literature. The review rated certainty very low to low, and durable glycemic control has not been established.

Summary of the Evidence

A narrow metabolic search identifies 41 publications on glucose, insulin resistance, or pancreatic islet outcomes: two reviews and 39 primary papers. The primary literature includes six human publications, 16 animal or insect studies, and 20 in-vitro or ex-vivo reports; three preclinical papers are counted in both laboratory and animal groupings. Human papers include randomized, nonrandomized, and case-report designs, and the database does not establish that every report represents a separate patient cohort. Studies of diabetic wounds or neuropathy without a metabolic outcome are excluded.

Human and clinical evidence

A randomized, double-blind sham-controlled crossover trial studied ten adults with type 2 diabetes across six treatment conditions. Near-infrared PBM lowered capillary glucose after treatment. The 100-joule dose per site showed the clearest reduction through 12 hours and a lower glucose area-under-the-curve measure; the 240-joule dose was not consistently better. Medication use was examined as a separate condition (Scontri et al. 2023).

A separate randomized study in 30 healthy adults used 670-nm red visible light before a glucose-tolerance test. It reduced the rise in glucose after the challenge, but it did not test treatment of diabetes (Powner & Jeffery 2024). A 2026 systematic review of four randomized diabetes trials reported reductions in fasting glucose, post-meal glucose, and HbA1c. The review reused the underlying trials rather than adding new patient groups, and rated certainty very low to low (da Rocha et al. 2026).

Animal evidence

Many diabetic or diet-induced rodent studies report improved glucose tolerance, insulin sensitivity, glucose levels, or pancreatic-islet measures after PBM. Some studies report no change in selected fasting-glucose or insulin-resistance measures, and protocols include different wavelengths, target tissues, and co-treatments. A bumblebee metabolic model also appears in the category and is not a mammalian diabetes model.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

Cell and isolated-islet studies often report improved glucose handling, cell survival, or insulin secretion under some stress conditions. Other experiments found no restoration of secretion or respiration, and responses varied with the type and timing of stress. Three mixed preclinical publications contribute to both the cell and animal counts.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The type 2 diabetes crossover trial used 830-nm near-infrared LED arrays at 100 or 240 joules per site over several bilateral limb-muscle groups, with glucose measured for 12 hours. The healthy-volunteer study used 670-nm red visible light for 15 minutes before glucose intake. Animal and cell studies use other targets and doses. No repeated-dose comparison establishes an optimal regimen or durable effect.

Interpretation

The small diabetes crossover trial found an acute glucose reduction after PBM, and a separate healthy-volunteer study found a lower post-challenge rise. These are direct short-term observations, but they do not show that PBM improves day-to-day diabetes control, lowers HbA1c, or can replace usual treatment. The much larger preclinical literature addresses mechanisms and animal outcomes, not lasting patient benefit.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow-to-moderate for short-term glucose reduction after PBM in adults with type 2 diabetes Low for sustained glycemic control or HbA1c reduction
Publications and records41 narrowly mapped articles

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

A sham-controlled crossover trial in people with type 2 diabetes found lower glucose after PBM, with the 100-joule condition showing the clearest response through 12 hours. A 2026 systematic review also reported lower fasting, post-meal, and HbA1c measures, but rated certainty very low to low. Larger repeated-treatment trials with longer follow-up would show whether these changes last.
